newsitem.title: USA: Key House Democrat seeks US bank reform safeguards.
newsitem.headline: Key House Democrat seeks US bank reform safeguards.

text.p: The ranking Democrat on the House Banking Committee urged that any relaxation of limits on U.S. banks be accompanied by additional safeguards to prevent disaster in the financial services industry.

Rep. Henry Gonzalez, in a letter to Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin dated Jan 30 and released Friday, also expressed concern about a proposal the administration is considering to allow commercial companies to own banks.
"Now and during my tenure as chairman, when a majority of the committee did not agree with my position, I did not stand in the way of legislation," Gonzalez wrote.

"Rather, I sought to the best of my ability to ensure legislation contained adequate safeguards to protect consumers and taxpayers," the Texas Democrat said. "Such protections are essential to any responsible revision of our banking laws."

Gonzalez suggested banks that enter other lines of business receive a reduction in federal deposit insuranbce coverage. Such a move "would impose market discipline on the bank while still protetcing average consumer deposits," he said.
Current rules on firewalls, legal separations between bank and non-bank departments, must be updated, he said.

Gonzalez also expressed concern about inadequate warning provisions in the Federal Deposit Insurance Corp Improvement Act and the potential for a troubled non-banking affiliate of a bank gaining access to the Federal Reserve's electronic payment system.
On the issue of mixing financial and non-financial companies, Gonzalez voiced strong reservations.

Most in Congress and the administration, though not Rep. Gonzalez, agree on the need to tear down laws separating banking from other financial service businesses. But there is little consensus about going further.

The administration is expected to release its own plan for banking reform in the next two months. Secretary Rubin is considering endorsing a recommendation from a task force headed by Under Secretary John Hawke to allow non-financial companies to own financial companies, people familiar with the matter have said.

That notion alarmed Gonzalez. "The prospect of Exxon Oil Company or Microsoft having ownership and control of Citibank or another large bank raises grave concerns about conflicts of interest and concentration of economic power," Gonzalez wrote. "I hope you will proceed very cautiously in this regard."
